title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Σ is a 'spatios' (Σ, ≤, c): an ordered set with extra structure. Figspatial(Σ), written Figéspat/Atop on these pages, is the set of 'spatial figures' X = (Φ, ρ), where Φ ⊂ Σ, ρ is an order on Φ, and Φ has a largest element X° for ρ. This set carries two induced relations: ⊴ (sub-figure) and |∘| (an incidence or support relation). An 'atelier spatial' is a set with two such relations satisfying axioms Atspat 1–3. Atspat 3 is a reconstruction axiom: from |∘| alone one builds a 'space' Σ_A of supports supp°_A, and the atelier must be canonically A ⊂ Figspatial(Σ_A).

The claim being proved (stated as an expectation on p.54). Let A ⊂ Figspatial(Σ) satisfy:
(1') A is closed downward under ⊴.
(2') Σ' = {X° | X ∈ A} is sup-dense in Σ: S = Sup{ξ ∈ Σ' | ξ ≤ S} for every S.
Then A, with the induced structure, is a spatial atelier, and Σ ≅ Σ_A canonically.

Proof on this page.
- Atspat 1 and 2 are called trivial.
- For Atspat 3, take α: A → Σ, X ↦ X° (the top element), and β: Σ → P(A), S ↦ {X ∈ A | X° ≤ S}.
- Then βα(X) = {Z | Z° ≤ X°}, compared with supp°_A X.
- And αβ(S) = {X° | X ∈ A, X° ≤ S}, compared with supp°_Σ(S).
- Conclusion: α and β induce mutually inverse bijections Σ_A ≅ Σ_Σ. Composing with the identification Σ_Σ ≅ Σ via supp°_Σ (from p.48) gives Σ_A ≅ Σ.
- On p.56 the canonical map A → Figspatial(Σ_A) (via Dév_A) is shown to become the tautological inclusion, so the order ρ is recovered ('On gagne!').
- Scholie: a spatial atelier is the same thing as a spatios Σ together with a ⊴-closed, sup-dense family of figures.

In modern terms this is an order-theoretic reconstruction lemma. A poset is recovered from a join-dense subset via S ↦ ↓S ∩ Σ'. Here it is lifted to a set of 'figures', i.e. ordered finite configurations with a top point. It serves the 1986 'ateliers' project: axiomatizing spaces through their figures.
errors: Only inclusions (⊂) are written for βα(X) and αβ(S), against supp°_A X and supp°_Σ(S), yet bijectivity is concluded. Either supp° is meant to be the generated closure, with equality implicitly intended, or a step is missing.
Sup-density (2') is needed to see that β(S) lands in Σ_A and that S is recovered from αβ(S). This use of 2' is not made explicit on the page.

ideas.what: Reconstructing the underlying space Σ from a down-closed family of figures whose top elements are sup-dense.
ideas.modern_name: join-dense subset / reconstruction of a poset from a basis (cf. Dedekind–MacNeille, ideal completions, sites and bases)

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'ateliers spatiaux': abstract sets with sub-figure and incidence relations, characterized as down-closed sup-dense families of figures in a spatios.
ideas.modern_name: closest: spaces defined by figures/plots (concrete sites); combinatorial models of spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; the ateliers framework itself appears only in the 1986 manuscripts

missed.claim: The 1986 'ateliers' theory gives an axiomatization of spaces via figures (Figspatial, supp°, Dév) with a reconstruction/equivalence statement (Scholie p.56). This page is one routine step of it. The framework as a whole is unpublished and unstudied, but this page adds nothing beyond a standard join-density argument.
missed.quote: d'où résulte que α et β induisent des bijections inverses l'une de l'autre entre Σ_A et Σ_Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with figure/plot-based notions of space (concrete sites, diffeological-type spaces, combinatorial stratified spaces). The comparison is only of historical interest unless the full atelier axioms prove novel.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification step: a reconstruction of a poset from a join-dense family, within an unpublished framework. Nothing here is unexpected for a specialist.
